1.explanation:
1. We import the Carbon React `Toggle` and its CSS.  
2. We render two toggles side by side:  
   - The first toggle has no visible labelText, only an `aria-label` prop.  
   - The second toggle uses `labelText`, which Carbon correctly associates as the accessible name.  
3. When you load this in Chrome on macOS 11.1 and turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5), the first toggle will not announce “Bluetooth.” VoiceOver will speak only the role “tick box” and its state. The second toggle will announce “Bluetooth, unticked, tick box.”  

This reproduces the bug that `aria-label` is stripped/ignored by the component and never forwarded to the underlying input element.
1.bug_scenario: In Carbon React Toggle v10.33.0, passing an `aria-label` to the `<Toggle>` component has no effect on the underlying `<input>` element’s accessible name. As a result, VoiceOver on macOS only announces the generic “tick box” role and state, instead of the provided label. The only way to provide an accessible name today is via the `labelText` prop, which renders a visible label. In the screen‐recorded example you can see two toggles stacked: the top one uses `aria-label="Bluetooth"` only (no visible label) and VoiceOver only speaks “tick box, unticked,” whereas the bottom one uses `labelText="Bluetooth"` and is announced correctly as “Bluetooth, unticked, tick box.”
